digest.component_or_area: bridge CLI and Python library — tracker sync operations
propositions: Legacy `reconcile` command remains non-mutating (dry-run default) while canonical `bridge sync` is mutating (live default), with explicit compatibility adapters bridging both behaviors.

Bridge operations (setup, check-access, fsck, status, preview, sync, pause, resume) are exposed through a unified Python library, CLI under `rebar bridge ...`, and MCP server with shared core semantics and no private reimplementations.
All installation paths (brew, pip, MCP-server/uvx) execute the same packaged Python bridge implementation, not repository-only helpers or ambient scripts.
Canonical exit codes are 0, 1, 2; legacy adapters translate historical 3, 4, 75 codes for backward compatibility with existing workflows.
Pause state is durably persisted with reason, mixed-version safe, and readable across fleet versions.
Tickets-branch CAS delivery is Python-owned in `src/rebar/_store/push.py`; no workflow-local retry loops remain, and destructive repair requires no `gh` CLI dependency.
